newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss assist probe of East German communist funds.
newsitem.headline: Swiss assist probe of East German communist funds.

text.p: The Swiss Supreme Court told two banks to give Germany documents it seeks to probe if funds of the old East German communist party were diverted to Swiss accounts, Switzerland's SDA news agency said on Wednesday.

The Federal Court in Lausanne rejected an appeal seeking to block Swiss legal assistance in the case, clearing the way for unnamed banks in Geneva and Basle to turn over records on accounts that had been blocked as a precaution in 1996, it said.
A court spokesman declined to comment. Its policy is to deal only with a small group of accredited journalists.

The Geneva bank has 5.5 million marks and the Basle bank 767,406 marks in deposits from 1990. German investigators believe the funds may have been diverted from the hardline East German SED party that ruled with an iron fist for decades.
The probe focuses on a German woman who headed the representative office of the All Goods International (A-G-I), which handled foreign trade for the SED, it said.

Identified only as G., she is suspected of transferring 7.58 million marks in SED funds to Vienna after communist rule collapsed in late 1989. Part of this may have subsequently been deposited in Swiss banks, it said.
German investigators tracking SED assets asked Switzerland in December 1995 to provide legal assistance in the case.
